title: Analytics schema staging gate and adaptive client fallback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Implement a staging-gate and adaptive fallback path to enable safe schema evolution for analytics/telemetry across SDK, CLI, and API ingestion points. The goal is to allow new schema fields and minor contract changes to be rolled out without consumer crashes or silent data loss, and to provide observability and automated migration assistance for producers that are out-of-date.

Background & motivation: We have several recent incidents where upstream SDK changes caused telemetry consumers (analytics pipelines and dashboards) to see malformed envelopes or missing required fields. Current ingestion either rejects the event (dropping data) or attempts a blind conversion downstream, which increases alert noise and complicates incident triage. We need a predictable, staged way to accept, validate, transform, and observe events across multiple schema versions while giving producers an automated rollback/fallback path.

High-level approach:
- Introduce a lightweight Schema Staging Gate service in front of the existing ingestion cluster. The gate validates incoming event envelopes against a targeted schema version set and applies non-destructive transformations when possible.
- Add an adaptive client fallback protocol: producers send X-RW-Telemetry-Client-Version and X-RW-Telemetry-Schema preflight headers; the gate responds with a short JSON notice in the 202/2xx body or with a standard JSON error when events are rejected. SDKs/CLI will read these and switch to a compatible envelope mode (legacy-envelope shim or reduced telemetry sampling).
- Implement a conversion bridge to translate between newer optional fields and legacy schema fields when a safe mapping exists. For unsafe or lossy changes, tag the event and route to a degradable path (low-priority partition) and emit a producer-facing diagnostic metric.

Design details:
- Version negotiation: Accept headers: X-RW-Telemetry-API v and X-RW-Telemetry-Schema v. If missing, assume v=1.
- Validation: Gate runs JSON Schema + business rules (required platform_id, timestamp sanity checks).
- Transformations: Use a transformation table stored in config service (keyed by source client version -> target schema) with deterministic conversions; fallback to shim when ambiguous.
- Backpressure & latency SLOs: Gate must add <3ms p95 to ingestion path. If the gate exceeds latency guardrail, it must drop to pass-through mode and emit telemetry_gate_overload metrics.
- Observability: Instrument counts for accepted_by_version, rejected_by_rule, transformed_by_rule, routed_to_degrade, producer_notice_sent. Add a per-producer rolling error rate and last_accepted_schema metadata to Console.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Gate deployed in front of ingestion with feature-flag controlled rollout.
2) SDKs (python/node/go) updated to send version headers and reactive fallback logic.
3) Conversion bridge implements at least three real mappings used by current clients.
4) Automated tests: contract-tests in CI for forward/backward compatibility; live canary validates no more than 0.1% dropped events for enabled producers.
5) Dashboard: new telemetry schema-migration dashboard aggregates per-producer compatibility and provides quick links to docs/upgrade steps.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0: Unit tests + contract tests, deploy gate to staging ingestion cluster behind a flag.
- Phase 1 (Canary): Enable for internal producers + 2 external partners (1%) for 7 days. Monitor rejected and degraded rates, latency, and storage pipeline backpressure.
- Phase 2: Expand to 25% of producers and sample full events for 48h to validate transformation fidelity.
- Phase 3: Full rollout once quality gates pass for 7 consecutive days.

Rollback & failure modes:
- If rejected rate > 1% or ingestion latency increases by >20% p95, revert gate to pass-through by toggling feature flag.
- If conversion errors spike for a specific producer, gate should mark that producer for manual review and send a diagnostic notice to the producer via the SDK callback endpoint.

Testing & validation:
- Create a contract-test harness that can fuzz event envelopes against supported schema versions.
- Add consumer-side integration tests (BigQuery / ClickHouse consumers) to ensure transformed events can be processed by downstream pipelines.
- Simulate producer SDK downgrade/upgrade sequences to validate adaptive fallback behaviors.

Docs & comms:
- Confluence page with migration guides and SDK change notes (link in comments).
- Email + Console notice for partner producers when we enable canary.

Dependencies: SDK release (ENG-120812), ingestion autoscaler work (ENG-119900), config-service feature flags (ENG-118004).
